title: Lovey Austin writing music at the piano
summary: As a child she watched Lovey Austin write music with a cigarette for the next act and decided to do the same, as she later did for Benny Goodman and Kirk.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Where did you run into Lovey Austin?

I ran into Lovey Austin when I was about 8 or 9 or 10 years old. I must have been pretty small because my brother-in-law used to throw me on his shoulder if I went to sleep in the theatre, and bring me home like that. He took me up there to see her, what she was doing. She had her legs crossed, with a cigarette in her mouth, playing and writing music for the next act. When the next act came on, the music was ready. She'd pass it out to the musicians who were going to play it. So I thought, I'm going to do that one day, and I did. That's how I used to work out my arrangements with Benny Goodman, when I was with Kirk.
Why did you want to do it?

Because it was amazing, that someone could concentrate like that - play, smoke a cigarette, with her legs crossed, and playing that music... And it comes easy after once you get on to it. I always wanted to do that... because it's so creative... I think there were two people inspired me because I wanted to do what they were doing.
